name: TREE-HAS-A-LIVE-RUN
reason:
TREE-HAS-A-LIVE-RUN: a run in progress executes this checkout and its .venv; changing either mid-run makes its result describe a tree that never existed.
Work in another worktree (git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/<name> <sha>), wait for the run, or stop it yourself: {python} -m dev_lab.dev.stoprun --pid <pid>.
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#tree-has-a-live-run (dev-lab)

name: BACKGROUND-SHELL-IS-BOUNDED
reason:
BACKGROUND-SHELL-IS-BOUNDED: a background shell outlives its purpose and its session; the reaper stops one at 50m unless the user granted more.
Start the line with timeout 50m <command> (compound: timeout 50m bash -c '<line>'). Longer: ask the user for the code; once they approve, {python} -m dev_lab.ops.consent grant <request.json> --code <code> (a longer bound names the request).
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#background-shell-is-bounded (dev-lab)

name: TRACKED-CITES-NO-EPHEMERAL
reason:
TRACKED-CITES-NO-EPHEMERAL: a task journal line is append-only: a cite of an ignored path written now is refused at commit and never repairable.
No door: rephrase the text before it is appended: cite a memory entry by name or the path as a <placeholder> shape (output/logs/<yy>/<mm>/<dd>/<kind>/) -- a written journal line is append-only, so this is the last point the agent can still change it.
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#tracked-cites-no-ephemeral (dev-lab)

name: SUBAGENT-NO-PUSH
reason:
SUBAGENT-NO-PUSH: publishing is the main session`s, and a skipped hook publishes what nobody checked.
Commit on your lane and hand the commit SHA back to the main session, which merges and pushes; measure the tests you touched: {python} -m dev_lab.dev.verify -- <paths>.
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#subagent-no-push (dev-lab)

name: HEAVY-IS-THE-MAIN-SESSIONS
reason:
HEAVY-IS-THE-MAIN-SESSIONS: heavy testing is the main session`s: it requests runs on the producer and reads the verdicts, and no local machine runs heavy tests.
Hand the request to the main session: commit on your lane and hand back the SHA; measure only the tests you touched: {python} -m dev_lab.dev.verify -- <paths>.
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#heavy-is-the-main-sessions (dev-lab)

name: CONSENT-CODE-FROM-THE-USER
reason:
CONSENT-CODE-FROM-THE-USER: a consent credential is written by the grant from a code the USER gave; a planted one forges the consent.
Write the request JSON under output/logs/<yy>/<mm>/<dd>/consent/, ask the user for the cluster code; once they approve, run `{python} -m dev_lab.ops.consent grant <request.json> --code <the code they gave>`.
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#consent-code-from-the-user (dev-lab)

name: COMMIT-HOOKS-RUN
reason:
COMMIT-HOOKS-RUN: a skipped commit hook routes around the wall it raised, so its cause is met again by the next commit.
Commit with the hooks: fix the cause the refusing hook names; a worktree with no venv: {python} -m dev_lab.dev.dep --bootstrap <worktree>.
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#commit-hooks-run (dev-lab)

name: BARE-TEST-INVOCATION

name: GIT-COMMIT-AMEND
reason:
GIT-COMMIT-AMEND: `--amend` rewrites HEAD, and on a shared lane HEAD may be another agent`s commit.
Land the correction FORWARD: read HEAD with git log -1 --format="%h %an %s", then commit the fix on top.
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#git-commit-amend (dev-lab)

name: GIT-STASH
reason:
GIT-STASH: `refs/stash` is repo-wide, so a stash is popped by whoever pops next -- possibly another agent.
Commit it on your own lane branch, or take a throwaway checkout: git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/<name> <sha>
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#git-stash (dev-lab)

name: GIT-RESET
reason:
GIT-RESET: `git reset` moves HEAD or the index of a checkout another agent may be committing in.
Unstage one path with git restore --staged <path>; undo a commit FORWARD with git revert <sha>; start over in a throwaway checkout: git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/<name> <sha>
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#git-reset (dev-lab)

name: GIT-STAGE-EVERYTHING
reason:
GIT-STAGE-EVERYTHING: staging everything in a shared checkout commits whatever another agent left unstaged.
Stage the paths you mean, then check: git add <path> <path>; git diff --cached --stat
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#git-stage-everything (dev-lab)

name: PUSH-FORCE
reason:
PUSH-FORCE: rewriting a shared ref invalidates every verdict taken against the old tree; --force-with-lease included.
Land the change FORWARD: git revert <sha> or a new commit on your own lane, then push without the force flag.
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#push-force (dev-lab)

name: PUSH-REMOTE-DELETE
reason:
PUSH-REMOTE-DELETE: a raw remote delete can lose commits held nowhere else.
a branch: `{python} -m dev_lab.dev.branchprune delete <branch>` (LOSSLESS-DELETE); one it refuses is MERGED, or LANDED by a declared `git merge -s ours` PR and then deleted (MERGE-OR-DELETE, D22: no tags).
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#push-remote-delete (dev-lab)

name: PUSH-NO-VERIFY
reason:
PUSH-NO-VERIFY: `--no-verify` skips the pre-push hooks (admission, the trunk proof), so the push publishes what no hook checked.
Push without the flag (no hook runs a test; the forge produces the part after the push), and to check a change first measure what you touched: {python} -m dev_lab.dev.verify
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#push-no-verify (dev-lab)

name: WORKTREE-BASE-IS-EXPLICIT
reason:
WORKTREE-BASE-IS-EXPLICIT: `git worktree add` with no commit-ish takes the current HEAD, which on a shared checkout is rarely the tree you meant.
Name the commit the tree starts from: git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/<name> <sha>
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#worktree-base-is-explicit (dev-lab)

name: WORKTREES-STAY-INSIDE
reason:
WORKTREES-STAY-INSIDE: a checkout outside its repository is outside every scan, ignore rule and search that repository runs.
Put it inside: git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/<name> <sha>; relocate: git worktree move <tree> .claude/worktrees/<name>. A family repo clones beside its siblings.
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#worktrees-stay-inside (dev-lab)

details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#bare-interpreter (dev-lab)

name: BARE-PYTHON
reason:

Use {python}, this worktree's own interpreter (main's is main-only); bootstrap a missing one with {python} -m dev_lab.dev.dep --bootstrap <worktree> (checked doors are agent-allowed, not arbitrary installers or code).

name: RECURSIVE-GREP
reason:
RECURSIVE-GREP: a recursive grep walks every git-ignored tree (.venv, output, target) and can run for minutes.
Search tracked files: git grep -n <pattern> [-- <paths>], or use the built-in Grep tool.
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#recursive-grep (dev-lab)

name: RECURSIVE-DELETE
reason:
RECURSIVE-DELETE: a raw recursive delete judges deletability by hand; on 2026-10-27 one took a MAIN checkout.
{python} -m dev_lab.dev.scratch clear --yes; dev_lab.dev.branchset --apply; dev_lab.dev.branchset --discard <branch> --approved <why>; detached: dev_lab.dev.worktrees --remove <name>; .venvs: dev_lab.dev.venvprune --apply. Else (never a worktree) ask the user.
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#recursive-delete (dev-lab)

name: REPORTS-LIVE-IN-MEMORY
reason:
REPORTS-LIVE-IN-MEMORY: a written report (audit, analysis, design, plan, findings) is not regenerable, and output/ holds only what a program can regenerate.
No door: write it with your Write tool as a dated memory entry: .claude/memory/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/<slug>.md with the MEMORY-SHAPE frontmatter (name, description, created; never accessed).
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#reports-live-in-memory (dev-lab)

name: WRITES-STAY-IN-THE-TREE
reason:
WRITES-STAY-IN-THE-TREE: outside every checkout nothing scans, ignores or cleans a file, so it outlives the session.
No door: write in the checkout. A program's artefact goes to output/logs/<yy>/<mm>/<dd>/<kind>/ and an experiment to scratch/ of the checkout you work in.
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#writes-stay-in-the-tree (dev-lab)

name: STATUS-VIA-DOORS
reason:
STATUS-VIA-DOORS: a raw post on tests/review-hold, tests/review or tests/security releases a head with no review or reason behind it.
Use the door that records why: re-run the forge's review of the head, {python} -m dev_lab.dev.forge review again <pr>; or forge security release <pr> --why "<reason>".
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#status-via-doors (dev-lab)

name: CI-CRON-NEEDS-CONSENT
reason:
CI-CRON-NEEDS-CONSENT: pausing or resuming CI rewrites a cluster account's crontab; an agent never does it on its own (user ruling 2026-11-16).
Read first: {python} -m dev_lab.dev.hpcaccount drift-fleet. Then the user runs it, or approves a consent plan on the cluster plus its account list ({python} -m dev_lab.dev.consent grant), then runs it with --credential <id>.
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#ci-cron-needs-consent (dev-lab)

name: HPC-THROUGH-THE-DOOR
reason:
HPC-THROUGH-THE-DOOR: an agent on an HPC login host or Slurm opens connections nobody budgets; a poll loop took the cluster's ssh down (2026-11-06).
Doors ({python} -m dev_lab.dev.<door>): TOTP host `sshhold open|run --code` (key-only: no code); deploy `hpcaccount <verb>`; verify: push, `forge queue|run show <sha>`; batch `lab_commons.hpc plan|submit|status|gather|retry|run`; clean `lab_commons.hpc clean`.
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#hpc-through-the-door (dev-lab)

name: REMOTE-WRITE-THROUGH-A-DOOR
reason:
REMOTE-WRITE-THROUGH-A-DOOR: a hand-written write to a remote host leaves no record of which door, host or reason changed it.
dev_lab.ops (--subject too): {python} -m dev_lab.dev.planrun preflight --plan P --steps S asks hosts; sshhold open --hours H --plan P --digest D (user's code); planrun run. Else opsserver <server> <verb>, hpcaccount. Spell out $VAR; read-only ssh is open.
details: docs-src/dev/refusals.md#remote-write-through-a-door (dev-lab)
